newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers more bullish on debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers more bullish on debt -- survey.

text.p: U.S. money managers over the past week put cash to work in their debt portfolios, slightly increasing their overweightings along the long end of the U.S. Treasury yield curve, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

"Money was put to work in extension trades as can be seen in the modest increase in the overweightings for intermediate and long durations," said MCM MoneyWatch economist Astrid Adolfson, who conducts the weekly survey.
Durations as a percentage of benchmark inched up to 108.1 percent in the week ended August 18 versus 107.9 percent in the previous week.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
Meanwhile, cash as a percentage of assets slipped to 3.21 percent from 3.25 percent registered the previous week.
"Even though rates are still higher than the recent lows, there was a slight decline in the number of persons saying the next move is to buy," Adolfson said.
Portfolio managers representing 43 percent of total assets in the survey indicated their next likely move would be to buy, down from 45 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" edged lower to 10 percent from 11 percent.
Forty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 44 percent the prior week.

Thirty-seven percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 36 percent in the previous week. Seven percent underweighted the sector for the fifth consecutive week, while the remaining 56 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 43 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 17 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
